paragraphs.text: Screenshot capture for the DSH composer: region capture and hide-window capture from the + menu, lan
ding in the chat input as an image attachment.
# dsh-screenshot-chat
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that adds a **Screenshot** entry to the chat composer's **`+` menu**, so a
region captured on your Mac lands in the input box as an image attachment.
## Features
- **One-click region capture** — opens the native macOS selection overlay (the same one as `⇧⌘4`), a
nd the selected region arrives in the current conversation's composer as an **image attachment**, re

ady to send with your next message. Pressing `Esc` or right-clicking cancels silently.
- **Hide-wind
ow capture** — hover the *Screenshot* row and a small toggle appears on the right (`○ Hide window`).
Turn it on and the window that is frontmost when you click is hidden first, then the selection over
lay appears; when the capture finishes or is cancelled, the window is restored and brought back to t

he front.
- **Mode is remembered** — the toggle state is stored in `localStorage` and survives page
reloads. While it is on, the menu item's description also shows the active mode, so you can see it w

ithout hovering.
- **Platform-aware** — the menu entry is hidden automatically on platforms without
`screencapture` (anything other than macOS).

Run `pnpm install` in the profile. With HMR enabled, config changes apply immediately; otherwise res
tart DSH. Host-side edits (`index.js`) take effect after touching the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (
any change re-composes the tree without a restart); client-side edits (`client.js`) are hot-replaced
by the client HMR poll.
## Usage

1. Click **`+` → Screenshot** in the composer.
2. Drag to select a region on screen.
3. The capture
appears in the composer as an image attachment — send it as usual.
To capture without the DSH window in the shot, hover the menu entry, switch on **Hide window**, then
click *Screenshot*. The window disappears during selection and comes back afterwards.

## How it works
### Host side (`index.js`)
Registers same-origin routes under `/.dsh-screenshot` on the host web server:

- `POST /capture` with body `{ "hide": true | false }`
- Runs `screencapture -i -x -o <tempfile>`, w
aits for the selection, then returns the PNG as base64 and deletes the temp file immediately. A canc

elled selection returns `{ cancelled: true }`.
- With `hide: true` it first resolves the **frontmost
process name** through AppleScript (System Events) and hides it (the equivalent of `⌘H`, with a sys
tem-level denylist — Finder, Dock, System Settings and friends are never hidden), waits for the hide
animation to settle (350 ms), then captures. A `finally` block restores and re-focuses the window w

hether the capture succeeded, was cancelled, or timed out.
- `GET /health` lets the browser half pro
be platform support (the entry is hidden off macOS).
Only one capture may run at a time. A capture that stays open longer than `timeoutMs` (default 180 s
) is terminated, and `osascript` calls time out after 60 s.
### Browser side (`client.js`)
Contributes a `screenshot` command to the `+` menu through `commandUi.register` (`kind: 'action'`, s
o a click runs the current mode). A document-level `mouseover` delegate spots the menu row carrying
the `data-dsc-icon` marker and mounts the hover toggle inside it, using native listeners and inline
styles so it does not depend on the menu component's internal class names. `mousedown` and `click` o
n the toggle stop propagation so the row is not selected.
The returned image is wrapped in a `File` and handed to `conversation.createDrafts` plus the compose
r's `addFiles` — the exact same attachment path as pasting an image, so previews, size limits, and u
pload encoding all run through the host's existing logic.
## Permissions (macOS)
1. **Screen Recording** — the first capture may prompt for authorization, or grant it under **System
Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen Recording** for the app running the DSH host. Without it, ca

ptures can come out as wallpaper only.
2. **Automation** (hide-window capture only) — hiding and res
toring the window uses System Events, so macOS asks to allow controlling System Events on first use;
the same switch lives under **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Automation**. Denying it leave
s plain region capture working; hide-window capture shows an authorization hint instead.
## Limitations
- Interactive region selection relies on macOS `screencapture -i`, so the plugin works on macOS only

; the menu entry hides itself elsewhere.
- Capture runs on the Mac hosting the DSH process, not on t

he machine running the browser. For a local deployment these are the same machine.
- *Hide window* h
ides whichever app is frontmost at the moment you click. If you switch to another app immediately af
ter clicking, that app is the one hidden.
